scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. If a proclaimed offender declaration is set aside, do the warrants, the Red Notice and the extradition fall too?
On twenty seventh October, twenty twenty six, the Delhi High Court, through a single bench of Honourable Justice Sanjeev Narula, answered that question.
scenes.shown: On 27 October 2026, the Delhi High Court, through a single bench of Honourable Justice Sanjeev Narula, answered that question.

scenes.dialogue: The petitioner faces a criminal case investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation. He joined the probe, then left India in two thousand eight.
scenes.shown: The petitioner faces a criminal case investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation. He joined the probe, then left India in 2008.

scenes.dialogue: The charge sheet recorded an address in Australia, but no attempt to serve him there was shown. In November twenty fourteen, he was declared a proclaimed offender.
scenes.shown: The charge-sheet recorded an address in Australia, but no attempt to serve him there was shown. In November 2014, he was declared a proclaimed offender.

scenes.dialogue: Now in Philippine custody and facing extradition to India, he challenged that declaration, and asked for a stay of the extradition proceedings.
The High Court held: Section Eighty Two needs proof of deliberate evasion. Unexecuted warrants are not enough, when his known overseas address was never pursued.
scenes.shown: The High Court held: Section 82 needs proof of deliberate evasion. Unexecuted warrants are not enough, when his known overseas address was never pursued.

scenes.dialogue: The offences alleged are outside Section Eighty Two, sub section Four, so he could not be declared a proclaimed offender. The proclamation was set aside.
scenes.shown: The offences alleged are outside Section 82(4), so he could not be declared a proclaimed offender. The proclamation was set aside.

scenes.dialogue: But this does not absolve him of his obligation to face the pending prosecution. And the warrants of arrest, a distinct process, remain unaffected.
The extradition treaty needs no proclaimed offender declaration. So no stay, and this ruling alone does not require withdrawing the Red Notice or the request.
